rpc: get_address_mempool_batch (batch the per-address mempool read)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/26

Adds `get_address_mempool_batch` — one request returns the mempool view for up to `MAX_BATCH_ADDRESSES` addresses under a single scan-rate charge and one mempool lock, mirroring the existing `get_balances` / `get_address_utxos_batch`.

**Why:** mempool was the only per-address read a wallet poll still made N times, each charged against the node's 30 balance/utxo-queries-per-minute scan cap. A multi-address wallet (especially on a CGNAT-shared egress IP) burned the budget and the next send failed with a rate-limit error. Batching collapses N scan slots into one.

**Already shipping in production.** Deployed on the public Seoul + Tokyo nodes, and consumed by the released wallets: [exfer-walletd v1.11.2](https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-walletd/releases/tag/v1.11.2), embedded in [exfer-walletd-desktop v0.13.1](https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-walletd-desktop/releases/tag/v0.13.1) and [exfer-walletd-mobile v0.5.4](https://github.com/exfer-stack/get/releases/tag/mobile-v0.5.4). Not a proposal — the code those builds talk to. It's called from `get_wallet_balance` via `get_address_mempool_batch_opt`, with a `-32601` fallback to the per-address path for older nodes.

Standalone node RPC — no dependency on the Phase 2 SSE work; split out of #25 for focused review. Backward-compatible: a client that doesn't call it is unaffected. `cargo check` green on `main`.
